name: Neutral link, open
summary: A neutral link drawn removed or open, showing the neutral conductor disconnected at that point.
description: The open neutral link shows the link withdrawn so that the neutral is disconnected. Drawings use it where a circuit is normally run with the neutral open, for example to isolate a spare or to segregate a neutral during a changeover, and on test procedures that show the link removed.

An open neutral on a live four-wire circuit can cause severe overvoltage on single-phase loads, so an open link in normal service needs a clear reason on the drawing. The symbol says nothing about the phase conductors, which may still be energised.
readingNotes: Ask why the neutral is shown open in service.
Check that phases are also isolated before working.
drawingChecklist: Note the reason the link is open.
Label the link with its circuit number.
distinction: An open neutral link is disconnected; the closed form shows normal continuity.
